verified_claims: The Composite DTM is a raster terrain model covering about 99 percent of England at 1m resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser return and removes surface objects from the DSM.
The 2022 composite merges Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is selected for the composite.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source surveys are resampled before merging.
The composite survey period runs from June 2000 to April 2022 and location-specific survey metadata must be consulted.
GeoTIFF data is supplied in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Heights are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn using OSTN15 for the composite.
Individual surveys entering the composite have stated vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The dataset exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS, WFS metadata and OGC API Features service roles.
Time Stamped DTM tiles are available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on survey requirements.
Time Stamped products retain survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal-model metadata by location.
The transformation used for Time Stamped data can depend on the survey period.
No exact TQ2892 filtered coverage response or candidate numeric WCS sample has been read back.
